Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Relative to estimated reaction functions in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler, the 25 bp cut alongside “balanced” risks reads as a small, forecast-based easing as inflation moves toward (but is still above) target, aligning with Svensson and Woodford’s inflation-forecast targeting perspective. The note that labor market conditions have eased and unemployment has edged up is consistent with the New Keynesian Phillips Curve view that a bit more slack should help disinflate further, yet the statement’s “somewhat elevated” inflation language and the decision to continue balance sheet runoff and maintain IOER/ON RRP settings to anchor short rates (Goodfriend on implementation) temper the dovishness. One hawkish dissent highlights residual upside inflation risk. Net: mildly dovish but constrained by still-elevated inflation and ongoing QT.
